key_insight: The paper shows that a quantum model’s circuit complexity is only meaningful if the available training copies can statistically support it, leading to a sample-supported expressibility law.
engineering_relevance: For quantum machine learning, this provides a principled way to choose ansatz size from data availability, reducing over-parameterization and improving model selection.
method: Derive a metric-entropy sample complexity bound for n-qubit states prepared with at most G two-qubit gates.
Define best G-gate approximation error d_G(ρ̂) and approximate circuit complexity C_η(ρ̂) for arbitrary sources.
Prove an adaptive oracle inequality that selects circuit complexity from data without knowing G in advance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports matching lower bounds and a sample law showing that, at trace-distance accuracy ε, M samples support only about G_supported ≃ Mε² gates, up to logarithmic factors and saturation near 2^n.
watch_item: The scaling is limited by logarithmic factors and ultimately by tomography saturation, so very high-complexity states may still be infeasible with finite copies.
paper_title: Quantum Occam Learning: Sample-Supported Expressibility for Circuit-Based Quantum Learning
